title: An interactive session's item stays out of the loop unless Mark moves it, and a session can pull an item into a worktree

story.as_a: Mark working ad hoc in an interactive session
story.i_want_to: keep the items my sessions open out of the loop unless I move them, and pull an item from the loop into a worktree here
story.so_that: ad-hoc work and loop work are one kind of record, and moving between them at any stage costs one command

rationale: PRD R2: ad-hoc work is a work item, moved between a session and the loop only by Mark, and section 8 assigns the end-to-end path 'an item moved from an interactive session into the loop and back' to this release. Release 3 already opens the item: US-52.18's work_item_open (POST /api/v1/work_items) creates it claimed by the session's holder with a stage row at implementing and its branch, and the MCP heartbeat opens it on a new branch. What release 3 does not do is keep it: a lapsed or ended interactive holder's claim releases through the normal paths (US-52.19) and the story returns to the queue for any runner (Progress.reclaim_expired_claim/3, lib/loopctl/progress.ex:2365, through Stages.follow_release/5, stages.ex:1731). This story adds that rule, migrates the items releases 3 to 6 released, and gives interactive sessions the pull US-52.44 gave runner sessions.

acceptance_criteria.description: When a claim held by an interactive holder is released, by the lease reclaim (Progress.reclaim_expired_claim/3), by the holder's end or by that holder's own unclaim, the release is not counted as an attempt and sets pending_move {target: {kind: interactive}, state: released, from_holder_id}, so the implement candidate query skips the item and MoveDeadlineWorker never expires that reservation.

An item reserved for interactive is claimed only by an interactive holder, through Progress.claim_story/3 or through work_item_open on its branch (US-52.18), and that claim clears the reservation; a runner_session or cloud holder, or a key with no holder, is refused {:error, {:reserved_for_move, story_id, target}}.

A data migration in this release writes the AC-52.46.1 reservation on every story that no holder holds, whose stage is neither done nor failed, and whose opened stage event came from US-52.18's open by an interactive holder; an ad-hoc item a runner holds at deploy stays with it, a second run writes nothing, and the run logs the count per project.

MCP work_item_pull {item, path} reads the item's newest unfenced checkpoint and unresolved fenced ones, fetches head_sha, adds a worktree on the item's branch at head_sha, checks then applies the diff with `git apply --binary`, and only then claims the item; when the claim is refused it removes the worktree it added and returns the refusal, and on success returns path, branch, head_sha, the applied files and the unresolved fenced checkpoint ids.

work_item_pull's default path is .claude/worktrees/<branch with / replaced by -> under the repository's top level; a path that exists and is not empty is refused path_not_empty before any git write, and a diff that fails `git apply --check` is refused diff_does_not_apply naming the rejected files before the claim, with the added worktree removed.

e2e/ path 'an item moved from an interactive session into the loop and back': a simulated interactive session (the MCP server over stdio with an interactive holder) opens an ad-hoc item on the sandbox repo with work_item_open, checkpoints an uncommitted change, moves it to loop with a grant minted through the hook from a synthetic UserPromptSubmit input, a host daemon resumes and pushes, a second grant moves it back here, and work_item_pull yields the runner's pushed head plus its last diff; an ungranted move is refused at both crossings.

test_cases.name: every release path of an interactive claim reserves the item (DataCase)
preconditions: three items opened by interactive holder I through WorkItems.open_interactive/3 (US-52.18); DISPATCH_MAX_ATTEMPTS unset
steps: expire the first claim and Progress.reclaim_expired_claim(tenant.id, story.id, epoch)
Holders.end_holder on I's second holder holding the second item
Progress.unclaim_story on the third as I
expected_results: each item has pending_move target interactive, state released, attempts unchanged, not escalated; none in candidates; reservations kept

test_cases.name: only an interactive holder takes a reserved item (DataCase)
preconditions: an item reserved for interactive on branch fix/a; runner_session holder R; interactive holder I2; a plain agent key
expected_results: {:error, {:reserved_for_move, _, _}} twice; I2 holds the same story with pending_move nil

test_cases.name: the release-7 migration reserves exactly the released ad-hoc items (DataCase migration test)
preconditions: before the migration: an unheld pending item opened by interactive holder I; an item opened by I now held by runner R; an unheld loop story placed by intake; a done item opened by I; a second tenant with its own unheld ad-hoc item
expected_results: the two unheld open ad-hoc items (one per tenant) reserved; R keeps its item; the loop story and the done item untouched; the second run writes nothing

test_cases.name: work_item_pull builds the worktree, then claims (node --test)
preconditions: temp origin with the item's branch at head_sha; stubbed fetch returning a checkpoint whose diff adds lib/a.ex, and one unresolved fenced id
steps: call it with a non-empty path
call it with a checkpoint whose diff conflicts
call it with the claim stubbed to 409 reserved_for_move
expected_results: worktree at .claude/worktrees/<branch> with lib/a.ex, claim POST last, fenced id returned; path_not_empty and no git call; diff_does_not_apply naming the file, no claim, no worktree left; the refusal returned and the worktree removed

test_cases.name: tool declaration and README row (node --test)
expected_results: declared and dispatched; the description names path_not_empty, diff_does_not_apply and reserved_for_move

test_cases.name: e2e: an item moved from an interactive session into the loop and back
preconditions: mix e2e with one host daemon and the MCP server started over stdio as an interactive session
expected_results: the move to loop with a hook-minted grant succeeds and the host daemon resumes and pushes
the move back here with a second grant succeeds and work_item_pull yields the runner's pushed head plus its last diff
an ungranted move is refused at both crossings

technical_notes: Built on exactly what release 3 creates: an ad-hoc item is a story opened by WorkItems.open_interactive/3 (US-52.18) with a story_stages row at implementing (Stages.open_started_in_tenant_transaction/4, renamed from open_for_change_in_tenant_transaction/4, lib/loopctl/delivery/stages.ex:305), branch on story_stages.branch (lib/loopctl/delivery/story_stage.ex:67), and an opened stage event whose actor holder is the interactive caller. Release 3 adds no interactive stage and no marker column, and this story adds none: the holder's kind at release time decides AC-52.46.1, and the opened event's holder decides AC-52.46.3.

Release paths: Progress.reclaim_expired_claim/3 (progress.ex:2365), Holders.end_holder/3's release of uncapped claims through unclaim_story/3 (progress.ex:1593; US-52.19 AC-52.19.8) and a holder's own unclaim_story/3 all read the claim's holder kind (US-52.13, US-52.14), pass cause :moved to Stages.follow_release/5 (US-52.43), and write the interactive reservation; US-52.43's :not_move_reserved predicate and claim refusal do the rest. A target of kind interactive is admitted by any holder whose kind is interactive.

work_item_open's claim (US-52.18 AC-52.18.4 takes an unheld item for the caller) goes through the same reservation check as Progress.claim_story/3, so a re-registered session takes back its own item and a runner never can.

The migration is a data migration after US-52.43's pending_move column exists; it selects through story_stage_events (event opened, actor_holder_id joined to holders.kind = 'interactive') per tenant on AdminRepo and writes pending_move only where it is nil, which is what makes a second run a no-op.

work_item_pull shares mcp-server/lib/worktree-diff.js with US-52.41 and runs git with execFile, as mcp-server/lib/client-context.js:45 already does; the claim is POST /api/v1/stories/:id/claim with the session's holder credential (US-52.13 AC-52.13.8), so release 3's held_by_other_holder and US-52.43's reserved_for_move refusals apply unchanged.

e2e: e2e/test/interactive_round_trip_test.exs uses US-52.45's hook script with a synthetic UserPromptSubmit JSON as Mark's typed command; it asserts an ungranted work_item_move answers 403 boundary_move_needs_mark at both crossings.
non_goals: Opening an ad-hoc item on a branch, its epic and the MCP heartbeat that opens it: US-52.18 (release 3); this story adds no second open route and no branch hook.
fleet_dash's display of ad-hoc items: fleet_dash reads factory_overview (release 5).
Closing an ad-hoc item when its branch merges: release 5's close verb, or the PR's existing delivery path.
Two sessions on one repo colliding: US-52.49's end-to-end path.

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.46.1: an interactive session that disappears loses its claim at lease end, and its item waits reserved for an interactive holder instead of being taken by the loop; its later checkpoints are stored fenced (US-52.42).
failure_modes.state: AC-52.46.4: the pulled worktree is built from the item's checkpoint in loopctl and the git remote; nothing is read from the source machine.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.46.3: the migration writes only where pending_move is nil, so a re-run after a failed deploy writes nothing; a repeated pull claims the item the caller already holds as release 3's idempotent claim answers.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.46.4: work_item_pull claims last, so a slow fetch or apply holds no claim.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.46.2: a re-registered session reaches its reserved item by re-opening its branch from any machine; fleet_dash reaches it by item id.

defaults: A lapsed interactive claim waits for an interactive holder indefinitely; it is Mark's own work (PRD R2), and fleet_dash's move verb or close verb ends the wait.
An ad-hoc item a runner took before this release stays in the loop; Mark moves it back if he wants it.
definition_of_done: On production after deploy: SELECT count(*) FROM story_stages WHERE pending_move->'target'->>'kind' = 'interactive' equals the migration's logged count.
